title: Bias Association Discovery Framework for Open-Ended LLM Generations
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, Bias Association Discovery Framework (BADF), measures previously known and unrecognized bias associations between religious identities and descriptive concepts that emerge in open-ended, long-form text generations (stories). It analyzes how different religious groups are characterized across various real-world contexts and sentiment constraints.
findings: The study found that for the religion category, all tested models consistently surfaced concepts related to faith, meditation, and mindfulness, particularly for Buddhism and Christianity. The sentiment of the prompt significantly influenced the generated associations; negative prompts led to more conflict-laden concepts (e.g., 'experiences interfaith tension'), while base prompts highlighted positive practices. The black-box setting revealed a broader variety of spiritual practices compared to the open-box setting, which tended to over-generalize concepts like 'devout' for Christians across all contexts. Different LLMs showed consistent patterns of associating specific religious identities with introspective or spiritual practices, though the context and granularity varied.
